input.rationale: Adding the concrete consequence of the accumulated queue, which the asserted account had only stated from source: on regaining the ability to commit in its term, the leader drains the whole queued read set in a single fast-path step, re-admitting every entry and broadcasting a heartbeat for each. The harness now includes TestAssuranceReadIndexQueuedDrainBurst, which queues 64 same-context retries on a two-voter leader before any acknowledgement, records the queue, then delivers the leader's own ack and node 2's MsgAppResp so the leader commits in its term and takes the MsgAppResp fast path that calls releasePendingReadIndexMessages. A local run shows the setup at pending=64, committed=0, in_term=false and the post-commit state at committed=1, in_term=true, pending=0, unconfirmed=64 with 64 heartbeat broadcasts from that single step. Submitted as a successor experiment for the same investigation; the account is revised only once the controller's receipt exists.

scope.description: Measure the drain burst: accumulate queued read requests on a leader that has not committed in its term, then let it commit in its term and record what the release path does with the whole queue in that one step.
assumptions: Real raft instance built with library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe) over voters {1,2}, so the leader becomes committed in its term once its own ack and node 2's MsgAppResp for the empty entry are delivered.
64 ReadIndex retries with an identical RequestCtx are submitted before any acknowledgement is delivered, so all of them take the queued path.

The commit is produced through the normal leadership path (self MsgAppResp stepped with From=1, then node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex), which is the call site that invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages; the harness does not call the release function directly.
excluded: Any claim about a network schedule or about a caller's retry timer; only the step-local effect is measured.
Whether the released reads are then confirmed: no heartbeat response is delivered, so the re-admitted entries stay unconfirmed.

experiment.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexQueuedDrainBurst builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2))), promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, clears the outbound buffers, submits 64 local MsgReadIndex messages with the same RequestCtx while clearing outbound traffic each round, and emits a setup event with the queue length, committed index, committedEntryInCurrentTerm() and unconfirmed length. It then steps a MsgAppResp with From=1 at lastIndex and node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex, which is the leader fast path that calls releasePendingReadIndexMessages, and emits the post-commit event with committed, in_term, queue length, unconfirmed length, the number of MsgHeartbeat messages produced in that step, and the node state.

comparisons.description: The single commit step empties the whole queued read set at once.
Every previously queued request is re-admitted into unconfirmedReads in that same step.
That one step emits one heartbeat per released request, so the retained queue also becomes a burst of outbound messages.

knowledge.assertion: releasePendingReadIndexMessages drains the queue through sendMsgReadIndexResponse, one response per queued message
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry

scope.description: Exercise the unexported readOnly confirmation path of package raft with ack values the live instance's heartbeatCtx never emitted, and record the two candidate consequences: an out-of-range slice in maybeAdvance, and confirmation of reads that the acking voter never observed.
assumptions: ack positions are supplied directly to readOnly.recvAck, standing in for MsgHeartbeatResp.Context values; this is an out-of-contract input, since the library's own follower path echoes the leader's context (see a167f4c33dc94f34b03ea29dbe7ec15a-knowledge-0).
ReadOnlySafe option; three voters (1,2,3) so the quorum position is the median of the stored acks.
The self-ack of the leader (id 1) is produced by heartbeatCtx() exactly as sendMsgReadIndexResponse does it.
excluded: Any claim that a legal cluster produces these inputs; the experiment characterises the code, not reachability.
Lease-based reads, which do not use the ack map.

basis.prefix: Each test builds a fresh readOnly via newReadOnly(ReadOnlySafe), admits one or two MsgReadIndex stand-ins through readOnly.addRequest(committedIndex, msg), self-acks with readOnly.recvAck(leaderID, readOnly.heartbeatCtx()), then injects peer acks with readOnly.recvAck(peerID, littleEndianUint64(position)) using values the leader never emitted, and finally calls readOnly.maybeAdvance(quorum.JointConfig with Voters[0]={1,2,3}). No raft instance, network or storage is involved; the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads are read directly, and the maybeAdvance call in the oversized case is wrapped in a recover to record whether it panics.

comparisons.description: When the quorum ack position exceeds the number of outstanding read requests, maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads out of range and panics.
One forged ack value combined with the leader's self-ack reaches a 2-of-3 quorum position, so both admitted reads are confirmed although voter 3 never received a heartbeat carrying position 2.

knowledge.assertion: no in-model producer supplies a Context the live leader never emitted, which is why this experiment uses an out-of-contract input

experiments.revision_reason: The first version named both probe events read_ack_probe and both setup events read_ack_setup, so the controller correlated each comparison against the other case's prerequisite and returned unknown. This revision gives each case its own event names (read_oversized_setup/read_oversized_probe, read_forged_setup/read_forged_probe) so each comparison has a single, unambiguous admission. No target code, prefix, injected input or assertion changed.

scope.description: Drive a real raft leader that cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements and repeatedly submit ReadIndex with the same RequestCtx, measuring the queued read state and whether it survives being deposed.
assumptions: The node is a legitimate leader: newTestRaft with voters {1,2,3} in the storage ConfState, promoted via becomeCandidate/becomeLeader, with the library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe).

No MsgAppResp or MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, which is the environment 'leader cannot obtain quorum acknowledgements'; outbound messages are cleared each round so growth is measured in raft state rather than in the msgs buffer.
Each round submits a fresh local MsgReadIndex with the same RequestCtx, which is the retry pattern the ReadIndex contract tells callers to perform.
excluded: Any claim about etcd's own retry policy or a particular caller's timer; only the library-side bound is measured.
Lease-based reads, which never enter the pending queue or ack structures.

basis.prefix: The test builds a real raft via newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it with becomeCandidate() then becomeLeader(), and emits a setup event recording state, term, committed, lastIndex, CheckQuorum, the read-only option and voter count. It then calls raft.Step 64 times with a local MsgReadIndex carrying the same RequestCtx, clearing r.msgs and r.msgsAfterAppend after each step, and emits the queue lengths. Finally it steps a higher-term MsgHeartbeat from node 2 to depose the leader and emits the queue lengths again to show whether the queued duty survives the authority transition.

comparisons.description: 64 same-context retries are all queued as separate pending read requests, matching the round count and showing no collapsing or bound.
After being deposed by a higher term, the node is a follower but the queued read requests are still retained, so the accumulation is not cancelled by the authority transition.

scope.description: Measure both admission outcomes of the ReadOnlySafe read path for a caller retrying ReadIndex with an identical RequestCtx: the queued path of a leader that has not committed in its term, and the admitted path of a leader that has committed in its term but whose follower stops acknowledging heartbeats.
assumptions: Both nodes are real raft instances built with the library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); the queued case uses voters {1,2,3} and the admitted case {1,2}.

For the admitted case the leader's commit is produced the normal way - the leader's own MsgAppResp is stepped from msgsAfterAppend and then node 2 acknowledges the empty entry - so committedEntryInCurrentTerm() becomes true without any artificial state.

After that point no MsgHeartbeatResp is delivered, which is the environment 'followers stop acknowledging'; outbound messages are counted and then cleared each round so growth is measured in raft state and broadcasts are counted explicitly.
excluded: Any claim about a particular caller's retry timer, and any claim about lease-based reads.
Reads that are eventually confirmed: the point is what the leader accumulates while they are not.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexPendingGrowth builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), promotes it, emits a setup event (state, term, committed, lastIndex, CheckQuorum, read-only option, voter count), steps 64 local MsgReadIndex messages with the same RequestCtx while clearing outbound traffic, emits the queue lengths, then steps a higher-term MsgHeartbeat from node 2 and emits the queue lengths again. TestAssuranceReadIndexAdmittedGrowth builds newTestRaft(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2))), promotes it, steps the self-ack messages out of msgsAfterAppend and then node 2's MsgAppResp for the empty entry so the leader commits in its term, emits a setup event including committedEntryInCurrentTerm(), then steps the same 64 same-context MsgReadIndex messages while counting MsgHeartbeat messages per round, and emits unconfirmedReads, broadcast count, pending length, confirmedReads and state.

comparisons.description: Queued path: 64 same-context retries are all retained as separate pending read requests.
Queued path: the accumulated requests survive deposition to StateFollower unchanged.
Admitted path: with the leader committed in its term but no heartbeat acknowledgements, 64 retries add 64 unconfirmed read requests.
Admitted path: each of the 64 retries also broadcasts one heartbeat, so retries cost outbound messages in addition to retained state.

knowledge.assertion: admission is per request and context-blind, and each admitted request broadcasts a heartbeat
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by deposition

result.summary: Added the concrete consequence of the accumulated queue, which the asserted account had only stated from source. New harness case TestAssuranceReadIndexQueuedDrainBurst queues 64 same-context retries on a two-voter leader before any acknowledgement (setup: pending=64, committed=0, in_term=false), then delivers the leader's own ack plus node 2's MsgAppResp so the leader commits in its term and takes the natural MsgAppResp fast path that calls releasePendingReadIndexMessages. Submitted as a successor experiment for the same investigation with three comparisons (pending==0, unconfirmed==64, broadcasts==64) and the release-site sources; the interpretation is deliberately not revised until the controller produces the receipt.
